Authority is never elected from session.players or player join order

environments.currentPlayer: the persistent browser player stored for this origin
notes: multi_screen loads the explicitly declared entries.game path; single_screen_multiplayer loads the explicitly declared entries.controller path
The SDK owns nickname input and nickname editing UI

The Authority gateway injects its default playmesh-app.js before playmesh-main.js; native App capabilities remain unavailable

notes: Loads the explicitly declared entries.game path

roles.description: The App host is the fixed Authority Client and separately participates as a member of session.players; its player position has no Authority meaning
The public display is Authority Client but is not a player
App or browser player that submits actions and receives messages

binaryTransport.connection: One lazy platform-managed Binary WebSocket per multiplayer game runtime, separate from the Session WebSocket
binaryTransport.channelIsolation: Many logical channels share the connection; data never crosses channel ids
binaryTransport.createAndClose: Authority only; Authority automatically joins a channel it creates

modes.authority: Non-Authority sends are reviewed by Authority; undefined passes, Uint8Array replaces, and throw rejects
modes.relay: Opaque bytes are routed directly to the target

delivery.send: Reliable queued frame; accepts one target, a target array, or no target argument for broadcast to all other online channel members
delivery.sendLatest: Accepts one target, a target array, or no target argument for latest broadcast; replaces only an older unsent frame in the same channel, sender and canonical target scope
delivery.multiTargetFanOut: One upstream binary frame is expanded by Core to all normalized target ids; Authority review receives targetPlayerIds as an array and runs once for the whole frame
delivery.startedAuthorityReview: Once an Authority handler starts, old and new reviews both continue and both decisions are honored

members.availability: The App session host only; browser players and App joiners can never register Authority
members.rule: Namespace is a routing label, not a security boundary. Use context.senderPlayerId and context.members[].id as trusted identities. Unknown named namespaces do not fall back to the default handler. The default route is last-registration-wins for compatibility; duplicate named routes are rejected

members.name: authorityPlayerId
members.behavior: Stable target and sender id for Authority in every Binary Channel

members.name: joinChannel

members.name: BinaryChannel
members.signature: {id, mode, send(Uint8Array), send(targetPlayerId | readonly string[], Uint8Array), sendLatest(Uint8Array), sendLatest(targetPlayerId | readonly string[], Uint8Array), onMessage(callback), onForward(handler), close()}
members.rule: send(data) and sendLatest(data) broadcast to every other currently-online member in this channel. onForward always receives targetPlayerIds: string[]. close and onForward authority behavior are restricted as described by the generated d.ts

members.name: onExit
members.rule: The host waits only for a limited time; save important state when it changes and use onExit only for business cleanup. The App owns final persistence.

authoritativeDataFlow: Preferred: game starts playmesh.main.sync on Authority, players submit semantic input, and SDK publishes versioned full snapshots
The App runtime that creates and runs the session is assigned authorityClientId before any player-order logic
The platform attaches senderPlayerId and the current SessionSnapshot
Authority handler validates the action and updates authoritative state
Authority returns targetPlayerIds using Player.id values and optionally SessionSnapshot.authorityClientId for the single-screen public display
Target pages receive the message through playmesh.main.game.onMessage
Opaque Uint8Array data uses playmesh.main.binary; the SDK owns the second lazy WebSocket, multiplexing, addressing and frame format
securityRules: Determine Authority only with playmesh.main.session.isAuthority() or SessionSnapshot.authorityClientId; never use players[0], join order or a first-player convention
Do not access PlaymeshBridge, chrome.webview, Core HTTP, WebSocket, share tokens or player credentials directly
Do not trust identity or final results supplied by action payloads
Treat Authority namespaces only as routing labels; every handler must validate the trusted context
Do not store credentials, player ids or game buckets in localStorage
Do not read data/json, cache/, .playmesh/ or another game package; use only URLs returned by Bucket upload for runtime files
Do not register authority service from a controller page

projectRules.managedManifest: main.json is edited through the visual manifest endpoint; id is immutable and raw file writes remain blocked
projectRules.capabilityRegistry: /dev/api/capabilities is the single metadata source for capability code, Chinese name, description, and App/HTML adapter status; generated AI prompts include this registry and the current declaration
projectRules.capabilityConsent: When capabilities.json.required is non-empty, the main SDK prompts on every App/browser game load. Rejection exits; unsupported capabilities are labeled but never block entry after consent; results are not persisted
projectRules.gameSdkVersion: main.json sdkVersion is required and must equal 4.1.0
projectRules.appSdkVersion: main.json appSdkVersion is required and must equal 3.2.0 or 3.3.0; new projects use 3.3.0
projectRules.gameEntry: main.json entries.game is required; it is relative to physical app/ and must explicitly identify an HTML file
projectRules.controllerEntry: main.json entries.controller is required for single_screen_multiplayer; it is relative to physical app/ and must explicitly identify an HTML file
projectRules.authorityEntry: main.json authority.entry is required for multiplayer games; it is relative to physical app/ and must explicitly identify a JavaScript file
